idea: Seasons come from Earth's tilted axis, which keeps pointing the same way in space as Earth circles the Sun, so each half of Earth leans toward the Sun for half the year.

parameters.name: day
parameters.why: A whole year round the orbit, starting at the June solstice.

parameters.name: tilt
parameters.why: From no tilt, where there are no seasons, to nearly twice Earth's own.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.why: Anywhere between the polar circles, north or south.

moves: Earth moves round its orbit with its axis leaning the same way, and the night side turns to stay away from the Sun; dragging Earth moves through the year.
steps: June: the north leans toward the Sun
December: the south leans toward the Sun
